179	class DatasetCatalog:
180	    def __init__(self, path):
181	        self.path = Path(path)
182	
183	    def entries(self):
184	        return json.loads(self.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")) if self.path.exists() else {}
185	
186	    def _normalize_entry(self, dataset, known_ids):
187	        return _normalized_record(dataset, known_ids)
188	
189	    def register(self, dataset):
190	        records = self.entries()
191	        if not isinstance(dataset, dict):
192	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset descriptor")
193	        identifier = dataset.get("id")
194	        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
195	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
196	        if identifier in records:
197	            raise ValueError("dataset already registered")
198	        entry = self._normalize_entry(dataset, set(records))
199	        records[identifier] = entry
200	        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
201	        self.path.write_text(json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
202	        return entry
203	
204	    def describe(self, identifier):
205	        records = self.entries()
206	        if identifier not in records:
207	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
208	        return records[identifier]
209	
210	    def search(self, query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None):
211	        if not isinstance(query, str):
212	            raise ValueError("query must be a string")
213	        if field_type is not None and field_type not in FIELD_TYPES:
214	            raise ValueError("field_type must be None or one of string, integer, number, boolean")
215	        required_tags = _normalize_tags(tags) if tags is not None else []
216	        required_owner = _normalize_owner(owner).casefold() if owner is not None else None
217	        words = {word.casefold() for word in query.split()}
218	        records = self.entries()
219	        results = []
220	        for identifier in sorted(records):
221	            entry = records[identifier]
222	            if field_type is not None and not any(field["type"] == field_type for field in entry["fields"]):
223	                continue
224	            if required_tags:
225	                available = {tag.casefold() for tag in entry.get("tags", [])}
226	                if not all(tag.casefold() in available for tag in required_tags):
227	                    continue
228	            if required_owner is not None:
229	                entry_owner = entry.get("owner")
230	                if not isinstance(entry_owner, str) or entry_owner.casefold() != required_owner:
231	                    continue
232	            matched_indices = set()
233	            matched = True
234	            dataset_haystack = (entry["id"] + "\n" + entry.get("description", "")).casefold()
235	            for word in words:
236	                hits = {index for index, field in enumerate(entry["fields"])
237	                        if word in field["name"].casefold()}
238	                matched_indices.update(hits)
239	                if not hits and word not in dataset_haystack:
240	                    matched = False
241	                    break
242	            if matched:
243	                results.append({"dataset": entry,
244	                                "matched_fields": [entry["fields"][index]["name"]
245	                                                   for index in sorted(matched_indices)]})
246	        return results
247	
248	    def dependencies(self, identifier):
249	        entry = self.describe(identifier)
250	        return [self.describe(key) for key in entry["depends_on"]]
251	
252	    def impact(self, identifier, max_depth=None):
253	        if max_depth is not None and (isinstance(max_depth, bool)
254	                                      or not isinstance(max_depth, int) or max_depth <= 0):
255	            raise ValueError("max_depth must be None or a positive integer")
256	        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
257	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
258	        records = self.entries()
259	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
260	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
261	        if identifier not in records:
262	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
263	        current = self._current_state()
264	        downstream = _downstream_index(current)
265	        reached = {identifier: [identifier]}
266	        frontier = {identifier: [identifier]}
267	        result = []
268	        distance = 0
269	        while frontier and (max_depth is None or distance < max_depth):
270	            distance += 1
271	            candidates = {}
272	            for node, path in frontier.items():
273	                for child in downstream.get(node, ()):  # unconnected records are never reached
274	                    if child in reached:
275	                        continue
276	                    candidate = path + [child]
277	                    if child not in candidates or candidate < candidates[child]:
278	                        candidates[child] = candidate
279	            if not candidates:
280	                break
281	            frontier = candidates
282	            reached.update(candidates)
283	            for child, path in candidates.items():
284	                result.append({"dataset": records[child], "distance": distance, "path": path})
285	        result.sort(key=lambda item: (item["distance"], item["dataset"]["id"]))
286	        return result
287	
288	    def upstream(self, identifier, max_depth=None):
289	        if max_depth is not None and (isinstance(max_depth, bool)
290	                                      or not isinstance(max_depth, int) or max_depth <= 0):
291	            raise ValueError("max_depth must be None or a positive integer")
292	        if not isinstance(identifier, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", identifier):
293	            raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
294	        records = self.entries()
295	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
296	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
297	        if identifier not in records:
298	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
299	        closure = _validated_upstream_closure(records, identifier)
300	        all_paths = _shortest_upstream_paths(closure, identifier)
301	        result = []
302	        for parent, path in all_paths.items():
303	            if parent == identifier:
304	                continue
305	            distance = len(path) - 1
306	            if max_depth is None or distance <= max_depth:
307	                result.append({"dataset": records[parent], "distance": distance, "path": path})
308	        result.sort(key=lambda item: (item["distance"], item["dataset"]["id"]))
309	        return result
310	
311	    def common_upstream(self, identifiers):
312	        if not isinstance(identifiers, list):
313	            raise ValueError("identifiers must be a list of dataset ids")
314	        targets = []
315	        for item in identifiers:
316	            if not isinstance(item, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", item):
317	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
318	            if item not in targets:
319	                targets.append(item)
320	        if len(targets) < 2:
321	            raise ValueError("at least two distinct dataset ids are required")
322	        records = self.entries()
323	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
324	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
325	        if any(item not in records for item in targets):
326	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
327	        closures = {target: _validated_upstream_closure(records, target) for target in targets}
328	        target_paths = {target: _shortest_upstream_paths(closures[target], target)
329	                        for target in targets}
330	        shared = set(target_paths[targets[0]])
331	        for target in targets[1:]:
332	            shared &= set(target_paths[target])
333	        # a candidate is dropped when another shared source depends on it, even
334	        # transitively through nodes that are not themselves shared
335	        merged = {key: entry for closure in closures.values()
336	                  for key, entry in closure.items()}
337	        downstream = _downstream_index(merged)
338	
339	        def nearest(source):
340	            return not (set(_shortest_downstream_paths(downstream, source)) & shared)
341	
342	        result = []
343	        for source in sorted(shared):
344	            if not nearest(source):
345	                continue
346	            source_targets = [
347	                {"id": target, "distance": len(target_paths[target][source]) - 1,
348	                 "path": target_paths[target][source]}
349	                for target in sorted(targets)]
350	            result.append({"dataset": records[source], "targets": source_targets})
351	        return result
352	
353	    def between(self, source, target):
354	        for endpoint in (source, target):
355	            if not isinstance(endpoint, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", endpoint):
356	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
357	        records = self.entries()
358	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
359	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
360	        if source not in records or target not in records:
361	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
362	        current = self._current_state()
363	        if source == target:
364	            return {"datasets": [records[source]], "edges": []}
365	        downstream = _downstream_index(current)
366	        forward = set()
367	        stack = [source]
368	        while stack:
369	            node = stack.pop()
370	            if node in forward:
371	                continue
372	            forward.add(node)
373	            stack.extend(downstream.get(node, ()))
374	        backward = set()
375	        stack = [target]
376	        while stack:
377	            node = stack.pop()
378	            if node in backward:
379	                continue
380	            backward.add(node)
381	            stack.extend(current[node]["depends_on"])
382	        chain = forward & backward  # every member sits on at least one source -> target path
383	        if not chain:
384	            return {"datasets": [], "edges": []}
385	        edges = []
386	        for node in chain:
387	            for parent in current[node]["depends_on"]:
388	                if parent in chain:
389	                    edges.append({"source": parent, "target": node})
390	        edges.sort(key=lambda edge: (edge["source"], edge["target"]))
391	        return {"datasets": [records[key] for key in sorted(chain)], "edges": edges}
392	
393	    def critical(self, source, target):
394	        for endpoint in (source, target):
395	            if not isinstance(endpoint, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", endpoint):
396	                raise ValueError("invalid dataset id")
397	        records = self.entries()
398	        if not isinstance(records, dict):
399	            raise ValueError("invalid catalog state")
400	        if source not in records or target not in records:
401	            raise ValueError("unknown dataset")
402	        current = self._current_state()
403	        if source == target:
404	            return [records[source]]
405	        downstream = _downstream_index(current)
406	        forward = set()
407	        stack = [source]
408	        while stack:
409	            node = stack.pop()
410	            if node in forward:
411	                continue
412	            forward.add(node)
413	            stack.extend(downstream.get(node, ()))
414	        if target not in forward:
415	            return []
416	        backward = set()
417	        stack = [target]
418	        while stack:
419	            node = stack.pop()
420	            if node in backward:
421	                continue
422	            backward.add(node)
423	            stack.extend(current[node]["depends_on"])
424	        chain = forward & backward  # nodes lying on at least one source -> target path
425	        critical = {source, target}
426	        for node in chain - critical:
427	            # a chain node is critical only when removing it breaks every source -> target path
428	            reached = {source}
429	            stack = [source]
430	            while stack:
431	                parent = stack.pop()
432	                for child in downstream.get(parent, ()):
433	                    if child == node or child in reached or child not in chain:
434	                        continue
435	                    reached.add(child)
436	                    stack.append(child)
437	            if target not in reached:
438	                critical.add(node)
439	        return [records[key] for key in sorted(critical)]

441	    def export(self, identifiers=None):
442	        if identifiers is not None and not isinstance(identifiers, list):
443	            raise ValueError("identifiers must be None or a list of dataset ids")
444	        selected = []
445	        if identifiers is not None:
446	            for item in identifiers:
447	                if not isinstance(item, str) or not re.fullmatch(r"[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*", item):

494	        closure = {}

496	        while stack:

498	            if key in closure:

501	            if entry["id"] != key:

604	                                  if before.get(name) != after.get(name))

607	                                "after": copy.deepcopy(after), "changed_keys": changed_keys})

633	    def preview_bundle(self, bundle):
634	        snapshot = self._snapshot_state(bundle)

637	        diff = self._diff_states(current, snapshot)
638	        sources = {row["id"] for row in diff["added"]}
639	        sources.update(row["id"] for row in diff["removed"])
640	        sources.update(row["id"] for row in diff["changed"])
641	
642	        # target id -> source id -> {"before"/"after": propagation explanation}
643	        reached_by = {}
644	        for side, state in (("before", current), ("after", snapshot)):
645	            downstream = _downstream_index(state)
646	            for source in sources:
647	                if source not in state:
648	                    continue
649	                for target, path in _shortest_downstream_paths(downstream, source).items():
650	                    propagation = {"distance": len(path) - 1, "path": path}
651	                    reached_by.setdefault(target, {}).setdefault(source, {})[side] = propagation
652	
653	        affected = []
654	        for target in sorted(reached_by):
655	            causes = []
656	            for source in sorted(reached_by[target]):
657	                sides = reached_by[target][source]
658	                before = sides.get("before")
659	                after = sides.get("after")
660	                if before is None and after is None:
661	                    continue
662	                causes.append({"id": source, "before": before, "after": after})
663	            if causes:

694	            removed_fields = [{"name": name, "type": before_fields[name]} for name in removed_names]

698	            if not added_fields and not removed_fields and not type_changes:

702	                for change in type_changes)

3	A local registry of dataset fields and direct dependencies, requiring Python 3.10+ and no third-party packages. It records descriptions and schemas, not the dataset contents.
4	
5	`python3 dataset_catalog.py describe orders` reads the included sample catalog. `python3 dataset_catalog.py dependencies daily_totals` returns the registered orders entry; queries are direct-only, not transitive. `python3 dataset_catalog.py impact orders` reports every registered dataset reachable downstream of `orders`; pass `--max-depth` (a positive decimal integer) to limit how many dependency edges are traversed. Each item holds only `dataset` (the same full record `describe` prints), `distance` (the fewest dependency edges from the start) and `path` (the id sequence from the start to that downstream dataset, both ends included, ties between equally short paths choosing the lexicographically smallest id sequence); the start is never listed, every downstream dataset appears once, and results are sorted by distance and then dataset id, with catalog key and dependency array order never affecting distance, path or ordering. Argument formats are validated before the catalog is read: a start id not matching the ID rule, or a depth that is not a positive integer, raises `ValueError`, as does an unregistered start. Before any result is produced the whole catalog is validated with `preview`'s metadata rules — a non-object top level, an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere raises `ValueError` with no partial result, even beyond the depth limit, outside the queried subgraph or when the start has no downstream at all; a registered leaf returns `[]`. A missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty catalog, an unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and the read-only query never writes files, creates directories or reads dataset contents; CLI failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2, success prints the result JSON and exits 0. `python3 dataset_catalog.py upstream daily_totals` is the mirror query along `depends_on`: it lists the direct and indirect upstream datasets of `daily_totals` (never the start itself), each item holding only `dataset` (the same full record `describe` prints), `distance` (the fewest dependency edges from the start) and `path` (the id sequence from the start to that upstream, both ends included). Every upstream appears once, sorted by distance and then by dataset id; ties between equally short paths choose the lexicographically smallest id sequence, and catalog or dependency ordering never changes the result. `--max-depth` (a positive decimal integer) keeps only records whose shortest distance stays within the limit, and omitting it returns the whole upstream closure; a registered dataset with no upstream yields `[]`. The start and its entire upstream closure are validated like a self-contained catalog — an invalid start id or depth, an unregistered start, a non-object catalog, and inside the closure an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle all raise `ValueError` with no partial result, and a depth limit never hides errors in farther upstream records, while records and relations outside the closure are ignored. Argument formats are validated before the catalog is read; a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty catalog, an unreadable file raises `OSError` and invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`. The query never modifies or creates files or directories and never reads dataset contents. `python3 dataset_catalog.py common-upstream --id orders --id daily_totals` finds the sources shared by several datasets: it returns an array sorted by source id, each item holding only `dataset` (the full record `describe` returns) and `targets` (every distinct target id, sorted, each with only `id`, `distance` and `path` — the fewest dependency edges from that target to the source and the id sequence from the target to the source, both ends included; ties choose the lexicographically smallest id sequence). Each target participates together with every upstream dataset reachable through `depends_on`, and a target itself is distance 0 with a one-id path. A source is shared only when every target can reach it, and a candidate that another shared source depends on directly or indirectly is omitted, so multiple mutually independent common sources are all kept rather than picking one by summed distance; when nothing is shared the output is `[]`. For the sample catalog, querying `orders` and `daily_totals` returns only `orders`, with distances 0 and 1. Repeat `--id` to name targets (duplicates merge; at least two distinct valid ids are required) and input order never changes the result. Argument formats are validated before the catalog is read: a non-list argument, a member not matching the ID rule, fewer than two distinct targets or an unregistered target raises `ValueError`; a non-object catalog top level or, inside any target's full upstream closure, an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle raises `ValueError` with no partial result, while records outside the target closures are ignored. A missing catalog file is treated as an empty catalog (so all targets are unknown), an unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and the read-only query never creates or modifies files or directories or reads dataset contents; CLI failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2, success prints the result JSON and exits 0. `python3 dataset_catalog.py between orders daily_totals` reports the directed dependency chain from `SOURCE` to `TARGET` along `depends_on` (B depending on A is the edge A→B): it prints exactly `{"datasets": [...], "edges": [...]}`. `datasets` collects every full record — the same object `describe` prints — that lies on at least one directed source-to-target path, including every connecting branch and paths of different lengths, sorted by id and without duplicates; branches leading off the chain and isolated nodes are never pulled in, and complete paths are not enumerated. `edges` lists only edges that sit on such a path, each item holding just `source` and `target` (the two ids), sorted by source and then target and deduplicated. It returns exactly `{"changes": [...]}`, sorted by dataset id, listing only records with field changes (no field change anywhere yields `{"changes": []}`); each item holds exactly `id`, `added_fields`, `removed_fields`, `type_changes` and `breaking`. `added_fields` and `removed_fields` hold `name`/`type` pairs and `type_changes` holds `name`/`before`/`after` pairs with the field name and its before and after types; all three arrays are sorted by field name in Unicode code-point order and are always present (as empty arrays). All fields of an added dataset count as added and all fields of a removed dataset count as removed; same-named fields are paired by their exact original names with no stripping or case folding, so a renaming is reported as one removal plus one addition. Differences limited to field order, description, tags, owner or dependencies produce no item (the field-order rule belongs only to the original `diff_bundle` comparison, which is unchanged). `breaking` is the feature's fixed verdict: `true` when at least one field is removed or at least one type change is not integer-to-number, and `false` otherwise — integer widening to number alone is therefore not breaking. The call never mutates the passed bundle or the catalog file, never creates files or directories, and never reads dataset contents; mutating the returned object affects neither the input bundle nor later queries. `DatasetCatalog.relation_diff_bundle(bundle)` is a read-only review of transitive dependency changes using the same complete-before/current-and-complete-after/snapshot semantics, normalization and two-sided dependency-graph validation as `preview_bundle` (a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty before state, an empty snapshot deletes every record, and validation runs even when no relation would change). It returns exactly `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}` comparing the reachable source→target pairs of the two graphs (B depending on A is the relation A→B, as in `between`): every distinct reachable pair participates at most once and each item holds only `source`, `target`, `before` and `after`, where `before`/`after` are `null` or an object holding only `distance` (the fewest dependency edges on that side) and `path` (the id sequence including both ends, ties choosing the lexicographically smallest id sequence). Pairs reachable only after the change are `added` (`before: null`), pairs reachable only before are `removed` (`after: null`), pairs reachable on both sides with a different `distance` or `path` are `changed`, and all other pairs are omitted — so metadata-only changes, alternative-path changes that keep the same shortest explanation, and isolated record additions or removals produce no item, while deleting a middle record reports the lost relation between its former ends. The two sides are queried independently with no cross-state path stitching, the arrays are sorted by `source` then `target`, input ordering never changes the result, and no relation change yields three empty arrays. The call never mutates the passed bundle or the catalog file, never creates files or directories, and never reads dataset contents; mutating the returned object affects neither the input bundle nor later queries. `DatasetCatalog.apply_bundle(bundle, expected_bundle=None)` commits a validated snapshot bundle as the complete catalog state — same-id records are replaced, new ids are added, records missing from the snapshot are removed, and an empty snapshot clears the catalog — and returns the pre-commit diff exactly as `diff_bundle` would have returned it (the `added`/`removed`/`changed` arrays sorted by id, with full before/after records and `changed_keys`). Normalization and snapshot validation match `diff_bundle`, the current catalog is validated with `preview_bundle`'s rules, and a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty before state; any validation failure raises `ValueError` before anything is written, so the catalog file keeps its original contents and a missing file or its parent directories are never created. The commit is all-or-nothing: with differences the full set of normalized records is saved atomically in the existing storage format (parent directories are created as needed), a save failure raises `OSError` leaving the original file untouched and a previously missing file still absent, and an empty diff returns the three empty arrays without writing a file or creating directories. When `expected_bundle` is not `None` it is validated with the same snapshot rules as the target and compared against the current catalog read for this call — normalized records aligned by dataset id, ignoring dataset order, object key order, unsaved properties and dependency order, while field order, tag retention/spelling/order and cleaned owner spelling count; a mismatch raises `ValueError("catalog does not match expected snapshot")` before anything is written, even when the target equals the current state, and an empty expected snapshot matches only an empty catalog. The call never mutates the passed bundle, mutating the returned records affects neither the input nor the saved catalog, and afterwards `describe`, `dependencies`, `search`, `impact` and `export` immediately reflect the new state; existing registration, import, export, diff and preview behavior is unchanged. `DatasetCatalog.merge_bundle(bundle)` incrementally merges an export-shaped `{"datasets": [...]}` bundle (any other top-level keys are ignored) into the catalog: each descriptor is added when its id is unregistered and fully replaces the same-id record otherwise — omitting `owner` or `tags` removes the old values and omitting `depends_on` stores an empty array — while records the bundle does not list are kept and nothing is deleted. It returns the same `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}` object `diff_bundle` returns, computed between the full catalog before and after the merge (so `removed` is always empty), with the same id sorting and `changed_keys` semantics. Descriptors follow registration's description conversion, field filtering, dependency sorting, tag cleaning and owner cleaning; dependencies may name existing records or other records in the same batch in any order, including forward references, and batch order never affects the result. The entire current catalog and the merged dependency graph are validated before anything is written: a non-object bundle, a missing or non-array `datasets` key, an invalid descriptor, a duplicate id in the batch, a catalog key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle — anywhere, including records the bundle does not touch — raises `ValueError` with no partial result, leaving the catalog file untouched and never creating a missing file or its parent directories. A missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty catalog; an empty batch or a merge whose normalized result equals the current state returns three empty arrays without writing a file or creating directories, and otherwise the full merged state is committed atomically once in the existing storage format, a save failure raising `OSError` with the original file preserved and a previously missing file still absent. The call never mutates the passed bundle, mutating the returned object affects neither the input nor the catalog, and dataset contents are never read; the CLI command `merge FILE` reuses `--catalog`, prints the result JSON and exits 0 on success, and prints JSON containing only `error` and exits 2 on failure. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None)` is read-only and returns a list sorted by dataset id; each item holds the same full record as `describe` under `dataset` and `matched_fields`, the field names hit by any query word in original field order without duplicates (empty when no field is hit or the query is empty). The query is split on Unicode whitespace, duplicate words do not change the result, and matching is literal substring matching after Unicode casefold — no regex or wildcards; every word must hit the same dataset, possibly across its id, description and different field names. An empty or whitespace-only query imposes no keyword restriction; when `field_type` is one of string, integer, number or boolean the dataset must have at least one field of that type while keywords still search every field name. A non-string query, or a `field_type` other than `None` and the four supported types, raises `ValueError` — arguments are validated before the catalog is read, so a missing or empty catalog still yields `[]` and never creates a file. `DatasetCatalog.search(query="", field_type=None, tags=None, owner=None)` also accepts `tags`: `None` or `[]` imposes no tag restriction, while a nonempty list requires the dataset to carry every listed tag. Tags follow the same type, stripping and dedup rules as registration, are validated before the catalog is read, and match whole tags by Unicode casefold only — no word splitting, substring, regex or wildcard matching. `owner=None` imposes no owner restriction; any other value is stripped of surrounding Unicode whitespace under the same nonempty-string rules as registration and must equal the record's stored owner in full after Unicode casefold — no word splitting, substring or wildcard matching. Records without an owner never match an owner filter; the owner filter is validated before the catalog is read. Records registered before owners existed are treated as having no owner and are never rewritten by a search. Keyword, field-type, tag and owner conditions all apply together; keywords still search only the original scopes (owner is not a keyword scope) and `matched_fields` still reflects keyword hits only. CLI errors are JSON and exit 2. Run `python3 -B -m unittest -v` for persistence, dependency validation and CLI tests.

# Dataset Catalog

A local registry of dataset fields and direct dependencies, requiring Python 3.10+ and no third-party packages. It records descriptions and schemas, not the dataset contents.

`python3 dataset_catalog.py describe orders` reads the included sample catalog. `python3 dataset_catalog.py dependencies daily_totals` returns the registered orders entry; queries are direct-only, not transitive. `python3 dataset_catalog.py impact orders` reports every registered dataset reachable downstream of `orders`; pass `--max-depth` (a positive decimal integer) to limit how many dependency edges are traversed. Each item holds only `dataset` (the same full record `describe` prints), `distance` (the fewest dependency edges from the start) and `path` (the id sequence from the start to that downstream dataset, both ends included, ties between equally short paths choosing the lexicographically smallest id sequence); the start is never listed, every downstream dataset appears once, and results are sorted by distance and then dataset id, with catalog key and dependency array order never affecting distance, path or ordering. Argument formats are validated before the catalog is read: a start id not matching the ID rule, or a depth that is not a positive integer, raises `ValueError`, as does an unregistered start. Before any result is produced the whole catalog is validated with `preview`'s metadata rules — a non-object top level, an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere raises `ValueError` with no partial result, even beyond the depth limit, outside the queried subgraph or when the start has no downstream at all; a registered leaf returns `[]`. A missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty catalog, an unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and the read-only query never writes files, creates directories or reads dataset contents; CLI failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2, success prints the result JSON and exits 0. `python3 dataset_catalog.py upstream daily_totals` is the mirror query along `depends_on`: it lists the direct and indirect upstream datasets of `daily_totals` (never the start itself), each item holding only `dataset` (the same full record `describe` prints), `distance` (the fewest dependency edges from the start) and `path` (the id sequence from the start to that upstream, both ends included). Every upstream appears once, sorted by distance and then by dataset id; ties between equally short paths choose the lexicographically smallest id sequence, and catalog or dependency ordering never changes the result. `--max-depth` (a positive decimal integer) keeps only records whose shortest distance stays within the limit, and omitting it returns the whole upstream closure; a registered dataset with no upstream yields `[]`. The start and its entire upstream closure are validated like a self-contained catalog — an invalid start id or depth, an unregistered start, a non-object catalog, and inside the closure an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle all raise `ValueError` with no partial result, and a depth limit never hides errors in farther upstream records, while records and relations outside the closure are ignored. Argument formats are validated before the catalog is read; a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty catalog, an unreadable file raises `OSError` and invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`. The query never modifies or creates files or directories and never reads dataset contents. `python3 dataset_catalog.py common-upstream --id orders --id daily_totals` finds the sources shared by several datasets: it returns an array sorted by source id, each item holding only `dataset` (the full record `describe` returns) and `targets` (every distinct target id, sorted, each with only `id`, `distance` and `path` — the fewest dependency edges from that target to the source and the id sequence from the target to the source, both ends included; ties choose the lexicographically smallest id sequence). Each target participates together with every upstream dataset reachable through `depends_on`, and a target itself is distance 0 with a one-id path. A source is shared only when every target can reach it, and a candidate that another shared source depends on directly or indirectly is omitted, so multiple mutually independent common sources are all kept rather than picking one by summed distance; when nothing is shared the output is `[]`. For the sample catalog, querying `orders` and `daily_totals` returns only `orders`, with distances 0 and 1. Repeat `--id` to name targets (duplicates merge; at least two distinct valid ids are required) and input order never changes the result. Argument formats are validated before the catalog is read: a non-list argument, a member not matching the ID rule, fewer than two distinct targets or an unregistered target raises `ValueError`; a non-object catalog top level or, inside any target's full upstream closure, an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle raises `ValueError` with no partial result, while records outside the target closures are ignored. A missing catalog file is treated as an empty catalog (so all targets are unknown), an unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and the read-only query never creates or modifies files or directories or reads dataset contents; CLI failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2, success prints the result JSON and exits 0. `python3 dataset_catalog.py between orders daily_totals` reports the directed dependency chain from `SOURCE` to `TARGET` along `depends_on` (B depending on A is the edge A→B): it prints exactly `{"datasets": [...], "edges": [...]}`. `datasets` collects every full record — the same object `describe` prints — that lies on at least one directed source-to-target path, including every connecting branch and paths of different lengths, sorted by id and without duplicates; branches leading off the chain and isolated nodes are never pulled in, and complete paths are not enumerated. `edges` lists only edges that sit on such a path, each item holding just `source` and `target` (the two ids), sorted by source and then target and deduplicated. The same id given for both ends, when registered, returns that one record and an empty `edges` array; two registered ends with no source-to-target path return two empty arrays, so the reversed direction `daily_totals` to `orders` is empty. The whole catalog uses `preview`'s metadata normalization and graph validation: a non-object top level, an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere — even outside the chain — raises `ValueError` with no partial result. Both endpoint formats are validated as existing id-rule strings before the catalog is read, and an unregistered end raises `ValueError`; a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty catalog so both ends are unknown. An unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and the read-only query never writes files, creates directories or reads dataset contents; CLI failures print JSON containing only `error` and exit 2, success prints the result JSON and exits 0, and catalog key or dependency array order never changes the result. For the sample catalog, `between orders daily_totals` returns both records plus the single edge `orders`→`daily_totals`. `python3 dataset_catalog.py critical SOURCE TARGET` prints a JSON array of the datasets that every directed path from SOURCE to TARGET passes through, with `between`'s edge direction (B's `depends_on` containing A is the edge A→B) and judging only the registered relations, never field lineage: each item is the same full record `describe` prints, every dataset appears once, the array is sorted by id, and no path set is enumerated. When a source-to-target path exists both ends are included; the same registered id for both ends returns just that one record, two registered ends with no source-to-target path return `[]`, and the reversed direction is judged by its own reachability. Every path counts regardless of length, so a merge point shared by all branches is included only while no longer bypassing path avoids it, and unrelated branches and isolated records never appear. Both endpoint formats are validated as existing id-rule strings before the catalog is read, and an unregistered end raises `ValueError`; a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty catalog so both ends are unknown. The whole catalog is normalized and graph-validated with `preview`'s rules — a non-object top level, an invalid descriptor, a record key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere raises `ValueError` with no partial result, even outside the queried paths or when both ends are the same. An unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and the read-only query never writes files, creates directories or reads dataset contents; CLI failures print JSON containing only `error` and exit 2, success prints the result JSON and exits 0, and catalog key or dependency-array order never changes the result. For the sample catalog, `critical orders daily_totals` returns both records. `python3 dataset_catalog.py export --id daily_totals` writes `{"datasets": [...]}` containing the selected datasets together with every upstream dataset reachable through `depends_on`; repeat `--id` to select more (duplicates merge), or omit it to export the whole catalog. Records are ordered dependencies first, breaking ties by id; exporting never modifies the catalog, and the output can be fed back to `register` entry by entry to rebuild the selected subset offline. `python3 dataset_catalog.py export-csv --id daily_totals` prints the same selection as a field-level CSV data dictionary for viewing datasets and fields together in a table: the fixed header is `dataset_id,description,owner,tags,depends_on,field_name,field_type`, every field gets one row and the dataset metadata is repeated across that dataset's rows. It reuses `--catalog`, repeatable `--id` and `export`'s selection semantics (no `--id` means everything, duplicate ids merge, the full upstream closure is included and input order never matters); datasets stay ordered dependencies first and fields keep registration order. A missing owner is an empty cell while missing tags prints `[]`; `tags` and `depends_on` are compact JSON arrays that preserve Chinese characters, with tags in stored order and dependencies sorted by id. Rows end with `\n` and cells containing commas, double quotes or newlines are double quoted with inner quotes doubled; newlines inside field names and descriptions are kept verbatim. An empty catalog or an empty selection prints only the terminated header. Selection arguments are validated before the catalog is read (a non-list argument, a non-string or invalid id, or an unknown id raises `ValueError`); a missing catalog file is treated as an empty catalog while a non-object top level raises `ValueError`, and the selected closure is normalized and graph-validated like `upstream` (invalid metadata, key/id mismatches, duplicate or missing dependencies, self dependencies and cycles raise `ValueError` with no partial output, while records outside the closure are ignored). An unreadable file raises `OSError`, invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and failures print JSON containing only `error` and exit 2; success prints the CSV directly and exits 0. `python3 dataset_catalog.py import FILE` imports a whole export-shaped bundle (`{"datasets": [...]}`) in one batch into the catalog selected by `--catalog`; dependencies may point at already registered datasets or at other datasets in the same batch, descriptors may appear in any order, and only metadata is registered — dataset contents are never read. Any validation failure rejects the whole batch, leaves the catalog file untouched and never creates a missing file or its parent directories; CLI errors are JSON with exit code 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py diff FILE` performs a read-only comparison: the catalog selected by `--catalog` is the before state and the `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot in FILE is the complete after state (a partial export still represents the whole after catalog and is not padded with current records, and records matching by id are compared directly without import's existing-id conflict rule). It prints `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}`, each array sorted by dataset id; `added` and `removed` hold full normalized records found only on one side, while each `changed` item holds `id`, `before`, `after` and a lexicographically sorted `changed_keys` list, and unchanged same-id records are omitted (empty arrays are still returned). Snapshot descriptors follow the same normalization rules as registration, so description conversion, field filtering, dependency sorting, tag cleaning and owner cleaning apply, unsaved extra properties and object key order are ignored, and tag spelling/order changes — including omitting `tags` versus `tags: []` — and owner changes (adding, removing, or changing the cleaned spelling, but not surrounding whitespace alone) count as changes, while dataset or dependency ordering alone do not. The snapshot is validated as a self-contained catalog: dependencies may use forward references but must stay inside the snapshot, and a non-object snapshot, a missing or non-array `datasets` key, an invalid descriptor, a duplicate id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle raises `ValueError` with no partial diff; an empty snapshot means the after state has no datasets, while a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` means an empty before state. The comparison never mutates the passed bundle, the catalog file or the snapshot file, never creates files or directories, never reads dataset contents, and an unreadable file, invalid JSON or failed validation prints JSON containing `error` and exits 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py preview FILE` is a read-only change-impact preview with the same before/after snapshot semantics as `diff`: it prints `{"diff": {...}, "affected": [...]}`, where `diff` is exactly the object `diff` prints and `affected` lists every downstream dataset reached from a change source. Added and removed records and every `changed` record are change sources — a description-only, tags-only or owner-only change propagates just like any other change — and when the diff is empty `affected` is `[]`. Each affected item (sorted by dataset id) holds only `id` and `causes`; a dataset appears once per side on which any change source reaches it along downstream edges, but a change source is never listed solely because it itself changed (it may still appear when another source reaches it). `causes` is sorted by source id and each cause holds only the source `id` plus `before` and `after`, the shortest propagation explanation on that side (positive edge `distance` and a `path` including source and target; ties choose the lexicographically smallest id sequence), or `null` when the source or target is absent or unreachable on that side; a cause with both sides `null` is omitted. The two sides are queried independently — a path valid only after the change is never stitched onto a before path — so a removed source can still affect retained or removed datasets in `before`, while an added source propagates only in `after`. Preview applies the snapshot validation of `diff` and additionally validates the current catalog's dependency graph: invalid descriptors, duplicate ids, duplicate or missing dependencies, self dependencies and cycles all raise `ValueError` with no partial result; a missing catalog file or `{}` is an empty catalog and an empty snapshot deletes every record. Preview never mutates its inputs, files or directories, never reads dataset contents, and its output does not depend on input ordering; file, JSON or validation failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py schema-diff FILE` is a read-only field-change review with the same before/after snapshot semantics as `diff` and `preview`: the catalog selected by `--catalog` is the before state and the complete `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot in FILE is the after state (a partial export is still the whole after catalog and is not padded, an empty snapshot means no datasets remain, and a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` means an empty before state). It prints `{"changes": [...]}`, sorted by dataset id and containing only records whose fields changed; records without a field change are omitted and when nothing changed it prints `{"changes": []}`. Each item holds only `id`, `added_fields`, `removed_fields`, `type_changes` and `breaking`: the first two arrays hold `name`/`type` pairs and `type_changes` holds `name`/`before`/`after` pairs giving the field name and its types on each side, and all three arrays are sorted by field name in Unicode code-point order (empty arrays are still present). Every field of a newly added dataset counts as added and every field of a deleted dataset counts as removed; same-named fields pair by exact name with no whitespace stripping or case folding, so a rename appears as the old field removed and the new field added, and changes limited to field order, description, tags, owner or dependencies produce no item. `breaking` is this feature's fixed review verdict — `true` whenever a field is removed or a type changes other than integer to number (the only non-breaking type change), and `false` otherwise, so a plain integer-to-number widening alone is not breaking. Both sides use `preview`'s normalization and full dependency-graph validation, so invalid descriptors, duplicate ids, duplicate or missing dependencies, self dependencies and cycles raise `ValueError` with no partial result, even when only other metadata would change; an unreadable file raises `OSError` and invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and every such CLI failure prints JSON containing `error` and exits 2. The command never mutates the passed bundle or any file, never creates directories and never reads dataset contents. `python3 dataset_catalog.py relation-diff FILE` is a read-only transitive dependency review with the same before/after snapshot semantics as `diff`, `preview` and `schema-diff`: the catalog selected by `--catalog` is the before state and the complete `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot in FILE is the after state (a partial export is still the whole after catalog and is not padded, an empty snapshot deletes every record, and a missing catalog file or one containing `{}` is an empty before state). It prints exactly `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}` comparing the reachable endpoint pairs of the two dependency graphs, with edges directed like `between` (B depending on A is the relation A→B). Every distinct reachable source→target pair participates at most once, and each item holds only `source`, `target`, `before` and `after`; `before` and `after` are each `null` or an object holding only `distance` (the fewest dependency edges from source to target on that side) and `path` (the id sequence including both ends, ties between equally short paths choosing the lexicographically smallest id sequence). A pair reachable only after the change is `added` with `before: null`, a pair reachable only before is `removed` with `after: null`, and a pair reachable on both sides whose `distance` or `path` differs is `changed`; every other pair is omitted, so field, description, tag or owner changes, alternative-path changes that keep the same shortest explanation, and added or removed isolated records produce no item, and deleting a middle record reports the lost relation between its former ends. The two sides are queried independently — no path mixes states — and the arrays are sorted by `source` and then `target`, so input ordering never changes the result; with no relation change the output is three empty arrays. Both sides are normalized and validated as full dependency graphs with `preview`'s rules even when no relation changes: a non-object catalog or snapshot, a missing or non-array `datasets` key, an invalid descriptor, a catalog key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle all raise `ValueError` with no partial result, an unreadable file raises `OSError` and invalid JSON raises `json.JSONDecodeError`, and every CLI failure prints JSON containing `error` and exits 2 while success prints the result JSON and exits 0. The command never mutates the passed bundle or any file, never creates directories and never reads dataset contents. `python3 dataset_catalog.py apply FILE` commits the `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot in FILE as the complete new state of the catalog selected by `--catalog`: records matching by id are replaced, new ids are added, records absent from the snapshot are removed (a partial export still represents the whole target catalog and is not padded with current records), and an empty snapshot clears the catalog. It prints the same `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}` object `diff` would have printed before the commit. The snapshot follows `diff`'s normalization and validation rules and the current catalog is validated with `preview`'s rules; any validation failure rejects the whole apply, leaves the catalog file untouched and never creates a missing file or its parent directories. The commit is all-or-nothing: when there are differences the full set of normalized records is saved atomically in the existing storage format (creating parent directories as needed), a save failure raises `OSError` with the original file contents preserved and a previously missing file still absent, and when there is no difference nothing is written or created. Pass `--expected FILE` to declare the catalog state the change was based on: FILE holds a `{"datasets": [...]}` snapshot that is validated and normalized exactly like the target snapshot and compared against the current catalog by dataset id (dataset order, object key order, unsaved properties and dependency order are ignored, while field order, tag retention/spelling/order and cleaned owner spelling count); unless the two match, the apply is rejected with `catalog does not match expected snapshot` — even when the target equals the current state — and an empty expected snapshot matches only an empty catalog. A `null` expected file is an invalid snapshot. Only metadata is handled — dataset contents are never read — and after a successful apply every query and export immediately reflects the new state. An unreadable file, invalid JSON, failed validation or a failed save prints JSON containing `error` and exits 2. `python3 dataset_catalog.py merge FILE` incrementally merges the `{"datasets": [...]}` bundle in FILE into the catalog selected by `--catalog` (other top-level keys are ignored): each listed dataset is added when its id is new and fully replaces the same-id record otherwise — omitting `owner` or `tags` removes the old values and omitting `depends_on` stores an empty array — while records the bundle does not list are kept and nothing is ever deleted. It prints the same `{"added": [...], "removed": [...], "changed": [...]}` object `diff` prints, computed between the full catalog before and after the merge, so `removed` is always empty. Descriptors follow registration's normalization and validation, dependencies may name existing records or other records in the same batch in any order including forward references, and batch order never changes the result. The whole current catalog and the merged dependency graph are validated before anything is written — an invalid descriptor, a duplicate id in the batch, a catalog key disagreeing with its id, a duplicate or missing dependency, a self dependency or a cycle anywhere, even in records the bundle does not touch, rejects the whole merge with `ValueError` semantics and leaves the file untouched. An empty batch or a merge with no normalized difference prints three empty arrays without writing a file or creating directories; otherwise the merged state is committed atomically once in the existing storage format. A missing catalog file is treated as an empty catalog, invalid JSON raises a JSON error, and failures print JSON containing `error` and exit 2 while success prints the result JSON and exits 0. `python3 dataset_catalog.py search "daily amount"` performs a read-only keyword search over dataset ids, descriptions and field names (dependency ids and field type text are not searched); the query is optional and `--field-type string|integer|number|boolean` restricts results to datasets having at least one field of that type. `--tag TAG` (repeatable, one tag per flag) restricts results to datasets carrying every given tag. `--owner OWNER` restricts results to datasets whose `owner` string matches the given value in full after Unicode casefold (surrounding Unicode whitespace is stripped first); records without an owner never match an owner filter, and the owner value is not searched by keywords. The two sample descriptors are `samples/orders.json` and `samples/daily.json`.

To create a separate catalog, run `python3 dataset_catalog.py --catalog .state/catalog.json register samples/orders.json`, then register `samples/daily.json` in that same catalog. import json
from pathlib import Path
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import unittest
from unittest import mock
from dataset_catalog import DatasetCatalog

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent


class CatalogTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.temp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory(dir=ROOT)
        self.addCleanup(self.temp.cleanup)
        self.path = Path(self.temp.name) / "catalog.json"
        self.catalog = DatasetCatalog(self.path)
        self.raw = {"id": "orders", "fields": [{"name": "amount", "type": "number"}]}

    def test_register_persists_schema_and_direct_dependencies(self):
        self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        self.catalog.register({"id": "daily", "fields": [{"name": "total", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": ["orders"]})
        self.catalog.register({"id": "weekly", "fields": [{"name": "total", "type": "number"}], "depends_on": ["daily"]})
        fresh = DatasetCatalog(self.path)
        self.assertEqual([row["id"] for row in fresh.dependencies("weekly")], ["daily"])
        self.assertEqual(fresh.describe("orders")["fields"], self.raw["fields"])

    def test_bad_dependencies_and_duplicate_fields_do_not_write(self):
        for item in ({**self.raw, "depends_on": ["unknown"]}, {**self.raw, "fields": self.raw["fields"] * 2}):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
                self.catalog.register(item)
        self.assertFalse(self.path.exists())

    def test_duplicate_and_unknown_dataset(self):
        self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.register(self.raw)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError):
            self.catalog.dependencies("missing")

    def _register(self, identifier, depends_on=None):
        self.catalog.register({"id": identifier,
                               "fields": [{"name": "n", "type": "integer"}],
                               "depends_on": depends_on or []})

    def test_impact_lists_reachable_downstream_with_shortest_paths(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily", ["orders"]),
                                       ("weekly", ["daily"]), ("report", ["orders"])):
            self._register(identifier, depends_on)
        result = self.catalog.impact("orders")
        self.assertEqual([(row["dataset"]["id"], row["distance"], row["path"]) for row in result],
                         [("daily", 1, ["orders", "daily"]),
                          ("report", 1, ["orders", "report"]),
                          ("weekly", 2, ["orders", "daily", "weekly"])])

    def test_impact_respects_max_depth_and_empty_leaf(self):
        for identifier, depends_on in (("orders", []), ("daily", ["orders"]),

--id and selection semantics (None = all, [] = empty, duplicate ids merge, full upstream closure
included, input order irrelevant); datasets stay dependencies first. Missing owner is an empty cell,
missing tags is []; tags and depends_on are compact JSON arrays preserving Chinese (tags in stored
order, dependencies sorted by id). Cells with commas, double quotes or newlines are double quoted
with inner quotes doubled, and newlines in field names or descriptions pass through; every line ends
with \n. An empty catalog or empty selection prints only the terminated header; read-only, errors
print JSON containing only error and exit 2.
python3 dataset_catalog.py search "daily amount"
Returns only orders with matched_fields ["amount"]; search is read-only.
python3 dataset_catalog.py search --field-type integer
Lists datasets having an integer field; an omitted query means no keyword restriction.
python3 dataset_catalog.py diff FILE
Compares the catalog (before) with a {"datasets":[...]} snapshot file (after, treated as complete)
and prints {"added":[...],"removed":[...],"changed":[...]} sorted by id; read-only, errors exit 2.
python3 dataset_catalog.py preview FILE
Prints {"diff":{...},"affected":[...]}: the diff result plus every downstream dataset reached from
an added, removed or changed source, with lexicographically-smallest shortest before/after paths;
read-only, errors exit 2.
python3 dataset_catalog.py schema-diff FILE
Reviews read-only field changes against a complete {"datasets":[...]} snapshot (catalog = before)
and prints {"changes":[...]} sorted by dataset id; each item holds only id, added_fields,
removed_fields (name/type pairs), type_changes (name/before/after) and breaking, arrays sorted by
field name; breaking is true for any removed field or non-integer-to-number type change;
read-only, errors exit 2.
python3 dataset_catalog.py apply FILE
Commits a {"datasets":[...]} snapshot file as the complete catalog state (same-id records replaced,
new ids added, absent records removed) and prints the pre-commit
{"added":[...],"removed":[...],"changed":[...]} diff; all-or-nothing, errors exit 2.
Pass --expected FILE to require the current catalog to match that expected snapshot first;
a mismatch prints {"error":"catalog does not match expected snapshot"} and exits 2.
python3 dataset_catalog.py merge FILE
Incrementally merges a {"datasets":[...]} bundle file into the catalog: listed datasets are
added or fully replace the same-id record (omitting owner/tags removes them, omitting
depends_on stores []), unlisted records are kept and nothing is deleted. Prints the same
{"added":[...],"removed":[...],"changed":[...]} diff as diff (removed always empty); an empty
or no-change batch prints three empty arrays without writing. The whole current catalog and
the merged dependency graph are validated before the atomic commit; errors exit 2.
